inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2026E = 9M-2026 actual net revenue 35,166 (Q1 10,253 + Q2 11,536 + Q3 13,377) + Q4 2026 guidance midpoint 17,000 (+/-3%, 3-Nov-2026). FY2026 is a 52-week year ending 2026-12-26; seven weeks remained at valuation. Y1 of the projection is FY2027.
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,661M = diluted weighted-average shares, Q3 2026 10-Q (basic end-of-quarter 1,640M). SBC is fully expensed in the flows so no SBC dilution is added. The rising path is GENUINE NON-SBC ISSUANCE, modelled per the method: (1) ~21M shares for the World Labs all-stock acquisition (~$8.2B) and the stock portion of Taalas (~$2.9B incl. $1.4B contingent), both closing Q4 2026; (2) customer warrants issued to OpenAI (Oct-2025) and Meta (Feb-2026), each for up to 160M shares at $0.01 (320M total, ~19% of the count), vesting on GW purchase milestones and stock-price targets -- the 10-Q says most market conditions had already been met at 26-Sep-2026, so vesting now turns on deployment. Base path vests 180M of the 320M (40/50/50/40M across FY2027-FY2030), i.e. roughly 7-8 of the 14 GW contracted. The engine takes a single share path, so the BULL case (all 14 GW deployed -> all 320M vest, ~7% more dilution than modelled) is overstated by ~7% per share and the BEAR case (few tranches vest) understated by ~8%; the probability-weighted figure is roughly neutral. The warrants' grant-date fair value ($14.25/sh, $4.5B unrecognised) is booked as a revenue reduction; that non-cash charge is NOT separately deducted here -- the dilution at market value is the economic charge, taken once through the count.
inputs.cash_basis: Cash and equivalents 7,404 + short-term investments 8,372 = 15,776 at 26-Sep-2026 (10-Q: 'cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments were $15.8 billion'). Debt is long-term debt, net 7,079 after the Aug-2026 $4.75B notes and repayment of the $875M 4.212% notes; no current portion. Long-term strategic investments (Sanmina stock, marketable equities) are left out of the bridge as immaterial (<$0.3/share); the up-to-$5B Anthropic investment is a commitment, not an asset, and is treated as a risk item.
inputs.sbc_source: TTM to Q3 2026 (FY2025 + 9M-2026 - 9M-2025). Cash-flow SBC add-back: FY2025 1,638 (AMD_Annual_FY2025.txt:2701) + 9M-2026 1,513 - 9M-2025 1,152 = 1,999. Equity-award tax withholding ('Stock repurchases for tax withholding on employee equity plans', financing): FY2025 607 (AMD_Annual_FY2025.txt:2772) + 9M-2026 1,836 - 9M-2025 447 = 1,996. AMD publishes no combined SBC-plus-withholding figure in its non-GAAP reconciliation, so the two lines are summed per the method. The withholding is at vest-date prices (4M shares withheld in 9M-2026 at ~$450 avg) and is inflated by the share price tripling; the forward sbc_pct_path anchors on ~8% FY2026E inclusive, 4% cash-flow SBC alone, and glides to 3.5%. Interest income: FY2025 215 (AMD_Annual_FY2025.txt:4014) + 9M-2026 336 - 9M-2025 137 = 414 (AMD_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:1450), stripped because net cash ($8.7B) exceeds 3x the owner-FCF base.
inputs.last_fcf_basis: TTM to 26-Sep-2026: OCF 9,123 (7,709 + 6,523 - 5,109) less capex 2,067 (974 + 1,845 - 752) = reported FCF 7,056; less SBC incl. withholding 3,995; less interest income 414 = owner FCF 2,647 (5.8% of TTM revenue 45,436). Note the TTM owner-FCF margin is depressed by the AI-ramp working-capital build (Q3 2026 OCF 1,202 on net income 2,428) and by vest-price-inflated withholding; the forward build is from components, not from this margin.
inputs.buyback_note: Actual financing outflow: 9M-2026 221 (TTM also 221 -- FY2025's 1,316 was all in 9M-2025). Repurchases have effectively paused while AMD funds AI infrastructure commitments; the flat-count convention for SBC is therefore NOT currently being funded by buybacks and is a modelling convention until repurchases resume.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: last Saturday of December (52/53-week); FY2025 ended 2025-12-27, FY2026 ends 2026-12-26
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-06T21:00:01Z regular close (Friday; valuation written Sunday 2026-11-08, no after-hours print)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD WACC. 10y UST ~4.1% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.3 (AMD's 5y raw beta ~1.9 is mean-reverted toward the mega-cap semi range now that the market cap is >$700B) = ~10.6% cost of equity; $7.1B debt at ~5% pre-tax is ~1% of capital and pulls the blend to ~10.5%. Applied identically to all three scenarios -- cyclicality and AI-capex risk are charged through the scenario paths and weights, not through a WACC premium (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases are immaterial relative to flows; lease cost stays inside EBITDA (treatment A: no lease principal deducted, no lease liabilities in net debt). The $13.3B of not-yet-commenced data-center leases to be assigned/subleased to partners and the $8.5B of partner lease/debt guarantees are contingent exposures carried as risk items, not as debt.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, scenario-weighted (dcf-methods routing: US operating company, tech hardware). The owner-fcf-adaptations file does not apply (USD/USD, no leases of note, no NCI, SBC-paying market). MID-CYCLE DESIGN: management guides >80% FY2027 revenue growth on the OpenAI (6 GW), Meta (~6 GW) and Anthropic (2 GW) MI450/Helios ramps; the base case haircuts that to +70%, decays to +30%/+12%/+2% over FY2028-30, then imposes an explicit -8% digestion year in FY2031 with the pre-SBC EBITDA margin dropping to 29% before recovering to a 34% mid-cycle level -- i.e. the model does not capitalise the FY2027-29 peak. Terminal caps are 15x base / 18x bull / 12x bear (cyclical range per the method), WACC 10.5% in all scenarios. D&A is depreciation only (FY2025 750; 9M-2026 666): the ~$2.3B/yr amortisation of Xilinx acquisition intangibles is non-cash and, as a stock deal without a tax step-up, largely non-deductible, so it is excluded rather than allowed to shield cash tax. Working capital is modelled on the CHANGE in revenue with a -22% capture (AMD's inventory + receivables build has absorbed 17-40% of each revenue increment in FY2022/24/25), so the FY2027 ramp consumes ~$8B of cash and the FY2031 downturn releases some. Cash tax ramps 14% -> 18% (FY2025 cash taxes 884 on ~4.0B pretax = 22% was distorted by catch-up payments; non-GAAP rate 13%; Pillar Two 15% floor; OBBBA R&D expensing lowers near-term cash tax). SIGNIFICANT NON-SBC DILUTION from the two 160M-share customer warrants plus the World Labs stock deal is modelled through projected_shares (see share_count_basis).
inputs.ai_infrastructure_commitments_note: Off-model exposures from the Q3 2026 10-Q and Analysis JSON: $48.8B unconditional purchase commitments (largely TSMC/HBM capacity), up to $8.5B maximum guarantee exposure on commercial partners' data-center leases/debt, $13.3B of not-yet-commenced data-center leases, up to $5B Anthropic investment, $1.2B warrant liability (non-cash). None is in net debt; the bear case is where they bite.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case 5-year forward revenue CAGR FY2026E 52.2B -> FY2031 121.2B (includes the modelled FY2031 digestion year). The equity CAGR is unusable as a growth proxy here: FY2022 equity jumped from 7.5B to 54.8B on the all-stock Xilinx acquisition, and FY2020 EPS/equity embed a $1.3B valuation-allowance release.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 60.9% vs revenue 28.8% / EPS 4.9%: divergence >30% in both directions. Cause is non-operating -- the Xilinx all-stock deal (FY2022) and the FY2020 deferred-tax valuation-allowance release -- so the equity series is flagged and NOT used as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs on FY2020/FY2022 -> FY2025 annual data (AMD_Metrics.csv; FY2025 ended 2025-12-27). Owner-FCF series: FY2020 777-274-78-5 = 420; FY2022 3,115-1,081-406-65 = 1,563; FY2025 6,735-1,638-607-215 = 4,275. Owner-FCF CAGR (39.8% 3yr) EXCEEDS reported-FCF CAGR (29.3%) because SBC+withholding grew slower than FCF off the depressed FY2022 base; this reverses in FY2026 where TTM owner FCF (2,647) is only 38% of reported FCF (7,056) as vest-price withholding balloons -- SBC cost is now taking a rising share of cash generation.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 +70% vs guided >80%: the OpenAI 1 GW tranche ships from H2 2026 and Meta/Anthropic start 2027, but second-source ramps, the HBM shortage and Helios rack-level execution justify a ~12% haircut. FY2028 +30% as further GW tranches land; FY2029 +12%; FY2030 +2% as the first hyperscaler digestion arrives; FY2031 -8% explicit downcycle (AMD's own cycles: FY2012 -17%, FY2015 -28%, FY2023 -4%); recovery 6% -> 3%. FY2030 revenue ~132B implies roughly 10% of a ~$1T accelerator TAM plus ~$30B of CPU/embedded -- a partial-success outcome, not failure.
base.margin_rationale: FY2026E pre-SBC EBITDA ~31% (9M segment op income 9,491 = 27% + Q4 guide 55% GM less 22% opex = 33%, plus ~1.9% depreciation). FY2027 36% on Data Center mix ~80% and opex growing ~35% vs revenue +70%; peak 38% in FY2028; mid-cycle 34% as Nvidia pricing, hyperscaler custom silicon and memory costs compress; 29% trough in the FY2031 downcycle (fixed R&D ~$10B+ on falling revenue).

bull.growth_rationale: Management's >80% delivered (+85%), all 14 GW of contracted capacity deploys on schedule, MI450/Helios wins additional hyperscaler sockets, EPYC keeps taking share from Intel. No downcycle, only a flat FY2031. FY2036 revenue ~223B -- a Nvidia-scale outcome at 40% pre-SBC EBITDA, still below Nvidia's current ~65%. Note this is also the scenario where all 320M warrant shares vest; the single share path understates bull dilution by ~7%.

bear.growth_rationale: FY2027 +45%: first GW tranches ship but 'up to' commitments are only partly drawn, Helios slips a quarter or two, China stays closed. FY2028 +5%, then an AI-capex bust in FY2029-30 (-15%, -12%) as hyperscalers digest and in-house silicon plus Nvidia's roadmap squeeze the #2; margins trough at 20% with ~$12B of fixed R&D on ~$60B revenue. The $48.8B purchase commitments, partner-lease guarantees and $5B Anthropic investment are the balance-sheet exposures this path tests. FY2036 revenue ~73B, 28% margin, 12x cap.

scenario_narratives.base: AMD becomes a durable but distant #2 in AI accelerators. The OpenAI/Meta/Anthropic agreements convert into roughly half of their 'up to' 14 GW over FY2027-30 (base vests ~180M of 320M warrant shares), MI450/Helios ships broadly on schedule, and EPYC keeps gaining server-CPU share. Revenue grows 70% in FY2027 (vs guided >80%) and 30% in FY2028, then the AI capex cycle matures: FY2030 is flat and FY2031 is an explicit -8% digestion year with the pre-SBC EBITDA margin dropping from a 38% peak to 29%, recovering to a 34% mid-cycle level. Working capital absorbs ~22% of every revenue dollar added (~$8B in FY2027 alone), SBC incl. withholding glides from ~5% to 3.5% of revenue, cash tax ramps 14% -> 18%. Terminal value is the lower of Gordon at 3% and 15x final-year owner FCF. The axes: how much of the contracted gigawatts actually deploy, how fast the first hyperscaler digestion arrives, and how much of the FY2027-28 margin survives Nvidia pricing and custom silicon.
scenario_narratives.bull: The >80% FY2027 guidance is delivered and then some: all 14 contracted GW deploy, MI450/Helios proves a genuine second source so additional hyperscalers (Microsoft, Oracle, sovereign AI) sign, ROCm closes most of the CUDA gap, and EPYC passes 50% server share. Revenue reaches ~135B in FY2028 and ~223B by FY2036 with pre-SBC EBITDA margins settling at 40%; the FY2031 cycle is a flat year, not a decline; terminal cap 18x. This is the scenario the current price needs. It also fully vests both customer warrants (320M shares) -- the single share path used by the engine understates that dilution by ~7%, so the bull value printed is, if anything, generous.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 'up to' gigawatt agreements are drawn slowly, Helios slips, the HBM shortage caps units and China stays closed under export controls (the MI308 precedent: ~$800M of charges in FY2025). FY2027 still grows 45% on tranches already in flight, but FY2028 stalls and FY2029-30 bring a classic semiconductor bust (-15%, -12%) as hyperscalers digest, Nvidia's annual cadence and in-house accelerators squeeze the #2, and Gaming/Client offer no offset. Pre-SBC EBITDA troughs at 20% on a ~$12B fixed R&D base; SBC incl. withholding stays 6%+ of a smaller revenue line. The $48.8B purchase commitments, up to $8.5B partner-lease guarantees and $5B Anthropic investment become real cash exposures. Recovery to 28% margins and 3-5% growth; terminal cap 12x.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear up to 25%: AMD's Data Center segment (~65% of FY2026E, ~80% of FY2027 per CEO) now depends on three AI customers whose commitments are 'up to' figures, layered on a semiconductor cycle AMD's own filings describe as prone to 'severe downturns', plus an unpredictable export-control regime and $48.8B of purchase commitments that are unconditional while demand is not. Bull down to 25%: the bull case needs several independent things to go right at once -- full GW deployment, Helios execution against Nvidia's annual cadence, ROCm adoption, and the AI capex cycle not pausing before FY2031 -- and the market-cap starting point (~$746B) already prices most of it.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF with SBC (including vest-date tax withholding) fully expensed, interest income stripped against the $8.7B net cash, and the two 160M-share customer warrants plus the World Labs stock deal charged through the share count. The model is deliberately mid-cycle-aware: it accepts most of the FY2027 ramp but refuses to compound it, building an explicit FY2031 downcycle and settling pre-SBC EBITDA at 34% rather than the 38% FY2028 peak, with a 15x terminal cap in the base. The gap to the market price is almost entirely about growth duration beyond FY2029 and the terminal multiple, not about the next two years -- base FY2027 NOPAT per share (~$12-13) is in line with where the street sits; the market pays ~35x that, the model pays ~14x on a 10.5% WACC.
key_risks_to_valuation: AI capex cycle duration: every extra year of 20%+ Data Center growth before digestion is worth roughly $25-35/share; the base assumes digestion begins FY2030
Warrant dilution path: 320M contingent shares vs 180M modelled; the bull case is overstated ~7% and the bear understated ~8% by the single share path
Margin durability vs Nvidia pricing and hyperscaler custom silicon: each 1pp of mid-cycle EBITDA margin is worth ~$4-5/share
China export controls: MI308 charges of ~$800M in FY2025 (partially reversed); a 15% revenue-share condition or renewed Entity List enforcement on THATIC JVs would hit Data Center directly

Balance-sheet commitments: $48.8B unconditional purchase commitments, up to $8.5B partner lease/debt guarantees, $13.3B uncommenced data-center leases, up to $5B Anthropic investment -- all outside net debt

Working capital: the -22% capture on revenue change consumes ~$8B in FY2027; if AI customers pre-pay (as some capacity deals allow) owner FCF front-loads and value rises; if receivables stretch, it falls
SBC measurement: vest-date withholding tripled with the share price; the glide to 3.5% assumes the equity-cost share of revenue normalises as revenue doubles
Terminal cap: 15x base owner FCF; the market's current ~100x TTM P/E implies it expects the cap never to bind
